note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, hour, price and lighting answer below comes from the City of Irvine's own pages: its pickleball page for the counts, the lighting and the reservation rates, its court regulations page for the rules about sharing a court, and each park's own page for the address, the hours and the amenities. Irvine states every published count twice, once in a sentence and once in an amenity list, and the three venues where the two records agree are published. Where the City is silent - on parking, on surface, on when the courts are busy - this page says so instead of guessing, and where the City disagrees with itself, both figures are quoted.

slots.parking: The City of Irvine publishes nothing about parking at any of these three parks. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, on the court regulations page or on any of the three park pages, and this site does not fill it in from a map. What each park page does carry is an amenity list, an acreage, a phone number and the hours, and those say what kind of site you are arriving at. All three are large community parks with a great deal happening besides pickleball. Mike Ward Community Park is approximately 22 acres, with two lighted basketball courts, three lighted racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, an amphitheatre, a fitness parcourse and three restrooms. Portola Springs Community Park is approximately 32 acres, with a community centre, two lighted softball fields, two lighted soccer fields, three lighted tennis courts, a concession building and two restrooms. Heritage Community Park is the largest at approximately 36.5 acres, with a community centre, twelve lighted tennis courts, three lighted soccer fields, two lighted ball diamonds, a lake, a splash pad and four restrooms. Every one of those lit fields is a reason other people will be at the park after dark, and the City states that its sponsored programmes have priority over all other use of the courts. Restrooms are stated at all three parks. A lot, a fee, a permit or a capacity is not stated at any of them, and the gap is recorded as a gap.
slots.peak_hours: Irvine states no peak times. What it states instead is a set of rules for how a court is shared, and they are the most useful thing on this page. All three parks are open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., daily, on the City's own park pages, and every one of the eighteen courts is lit, so the window is sixteen hours long and does not shrink at dusk. Within that window the court regulations say: "Open courts are on a first-come, first-serve basis. Please use the waiting board where available." When others are waiting, doubles is limited to 60 minutes and singles to 30, warm-up included, and "all players and group members must vacate the court when the time limit expires". If nobody is waiting you may carry on. Groups "may not camp on a court". Two courts at each of the two largest venues run on a different clock. Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs can be reserved online "between the hours of 7 a.m. to noon, and 4 to 10 p.m.", in one- or two-hour blocks, one reservation per person per day; residents may book five days ahead and non-residents three. The City's choice of those windows is the nearest thing it publishes to a statement of when its courts are wanted: mornings, and after four. Whenever nobody has booked them the reservable courts revert to drop-in play, and a drop-in player must leave "if a reservation holder arrives during their allotted time". The City adds that its sponsored programmes - the lessons it runs at all three parks and the Irvine Team Pickleball league at Portola Springs - have priority over all other use.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Irvine. No park page says what the courts are made of, the regulations page does not, and the pickleball page does not, so this site records nothing. What the City does write, consistently, is the word lit: "eight lit pickleball courts", "six lit pickleball courts" and "four lit pickleball courts" on the pickleball page, and "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts", "6 Lighted Pickleball Courts" and "4 Lighted Pickleball Courts" in the amenity lists, so the lighting of every published court in this city rests on two City records rather than one. The other thing the City is careful about is the difference between a pickleball court and a tennis court with pickleball on it. The eighteen courts here are all counted as pickleball courts. Separately, the City lists hybrid tennis-and-pickleball courts at a set of parks that includes Heritage, and gives only a city-wide total for them - ten on the pickleball page, nine on the regulations page - never a per-park figure, so none is added to any venue here. On a tennis court the regulations are explicit: "Tennis courts are designated solely for tennis use", pickleball may be played only when no tennis player is waiting, and if tennis players arrive "those playing pickleball or badminton must vacate the court". On the eighteen dedicated courts no such rule applies. Tennis shoes are required on every City court, and pets, food, bicycles and skateboards are not permitted on them.
slots.local_scene: Eighteen verified courts across three parks, every one lit in the City's own word, every park open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Irvine is the first California city on this site. It is also the second operator here, after Mesa, to publish an hourly price for reserving a court, and the first to publish two of them: Courts #3 and #4 at Mike Ward Community Park and Courts #5 and #6 at Portola Springs Community Park can be booked at "Resident Rate: $17/hr" and "Non-Resident Rate: $19/hr". The other fourteen courts are first come, first served and the City states no price for them. The word free appears on none of its pages, so no Irvine venue reaches the free page. The City runs junior, adult and private lessons at all three parks through contract instructors, and a league, Irvine Team Pickleball, at Portola Springs: eight teams, a seven-week round robin and three-week playoffs, self-rated at 3.5, $490 per team per season. A fourth venue is missing, and it is missing because the City contradicts itself. The pickleball page and the regulations page both give Los Olivos Community Park "two lit pickleball courts"; the park's own amenity list gives "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts". This site's rule is that the record stating a number publishes, and that rule cannot choose between two numbers, so Los Olivos is named here and not listed. The City's pages disagree about the citywide total as well. The regulations page says "The City of Irvine has 96 public tennis courts, 12 public pickleball courts, and 8 public hybrid tennis/pickleball courts"; the per-park sentence on the pickleball page adds to twenty, and the regulations page's own list of lit courts leaves Heritage out altogether. Knollcrest, San Carlo, Turtle Rock and University carry hybrid courts under a city-wide aggregate with no per-park count, so they are not venues here. The City also says it "is evaluating building pickleball courts at the Great Park".

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Mike Ward Community Park has eight lit pickleball courts, the largest set in Irvine, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily in a 22-acre park with three restrooms, lighted basketball and racquetball courts and a sand volleyball court. Six courts are first come, first served; Courts #3 and #4 can be booked online at $17 an hour for residents and $19 for non-residents.

best_for.heading: Best if you want organised play
best_for.text: Portola Springs Community Park has six lit courts and is the home of Irvine Team Pickleball, the City's league: eight teams, a seven-week round robin, three weeks of playoffs, self-rated 3.5, $490 per team per season. Courts #5 and #6 are reservable at the same $17 and $19 rates as Mike Ward, and the City's contract instructors teach lessons here. Open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to turn up and play
best_for.text: Heritage Community Park has four lit courts and no reservation system: every court is first come, first served under the City's regulations, with a waiting board and a 60-minute doubles limit when others are waiting. It is the largest park of the three at 36.5 acres, with twelve lighted tennis courts, a lake, a splash pad and four restrooms, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Irvine have?
faqs.a: We have verified 18 across three City parks: eight at Mike Ward Community Park, six at Portola Springs Community Park and four at Heritage Community Park, each count stated twice by the City. The City itself gives several totals - "12 public pickleball courts" on its regulations page, twenty by adding its own per-park sentence - and a fourth park, Los Olivos, is credited with two courts on two pages and three on a third.

All eighteen published courts, and the City states it twice for each venue: "eight lit pickleball courts" and "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts" at Mike Ward, and the same pairing at Portola Springs with six and Heritage with four. All three parks are open until 10 p.m. daily, so the lights are attached to a real evening window.

6 a.m. to 10 p.m., daily, at all three parks, on each park's own page. Within those hours the City's court regulations apply: open courts are first come, first served, doubles is limited to 60 minutes and singles to 30 when others are waiting, and the reservable courts can be booked between 7 a.m. and noon and 4 and 10 p.m.

faqs.q: Why is Los Olivos Community Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because the City states two different counts for it. The pickleball page and the court regulations page both say "two lit pickleball courts"; the park's own amenity list says "3 Lighted Pickleball Courts". This site publishes the number the operator states, and cannot publish when the operator states two. The address, 101 Alfonso, resolves and the courts are lit; it fails on the count alone.

Only four courts are reservable: #3 and #4 at Mike Ward and #5 and #6 at Portola Springs. Bookings are made online, residents up to five days ahead and non-residents three, in one- or two-hour blocks between 7 a.m. and noon and 4 and 10 p.m. The City says the courts can be used for drop-in play when nobody has booked, and that drop-in players must vacate when a reservation holder arrives.

"Reservations can be made in one or two hour increments, with individuals allowed to have one reservation per day." "Courts can be reserved Monday through Sunday, between the hours of 7 a.m. to noon, and 4 to 10 p.m." The reservable courts "can be used for drop-in play if there is no reservation or if a reservation no-shows"; "Please immediately vacate the court if a reservation holder arrives during their allotted time." Lessons "at Mike Ward Community Park, Portola Springs Community Park and Heritage Park".
